note: Reworded-fact probes for the research-group demo (spec 02, section 9.2), in the same shape as data/demo/probes.json. 'facts' are restricted items of this demo's answer key (data/lab/ground_truth.json 'restricted'), restated so the key-term check and the judge have something to look for. 'rewordings' are catchable by the key terms of their own fact; 'hardRewordings' use none of them and are for the model judge only. 'evalSegments' is the classifier evaluation set: it is ingested into a scratch workspace by the evaluation script and is never part of the live demo sources. mustGroups holds zero-based indexes into termGroups. Categories are the three the classifier knows: a biosafety lapse is filed under health as the nearest of them. All people and organisations are fictional.

facts.fact: Two flow cells are prepaid for the January run and are held at the sequencing core for this lab.
rewordings: The two flow cells for the January run were paid in advance, there is nothing left to pay there.
Both January flow cells are already paid for and the invoice is settled.
Do not budget for flow cells in January, they are prepaid.
hardRewordings: The two cells for the first run of the new year are already covered, nothing more goes out for them.

facts.fact: The data shared with Helix Agritech is under embargo until 30 June 2027.
rewordings: The Helix data cannot be published before 30 June 2027.
Helix Agritech terms put the shared data under embargo until mid 2027.
Nothing from the Helix dataset can go into a paper until the embargo ends in June 2027.
hardRewordings: Our industry partner holds the shared results back from any paper until the middle of 2027.

facts.fact: Helix Agritech pays a data access fee of Rs 4,50,000 on delivery of the first dataset, and it is not split into two parts.
rewordings: Helix pays the data access fee on delivery of the first dataset.
The access fee from Helix is Rs 4,50,000 and it will not be split.
Helix Agritech owes 450000 as the access fee for the first dataset.
hardRewordings: The partner company transfers the agreed sum for the data in one instalment when the first delivery goes out.

facts.fact: The flow-cell and reagent standing order must be raised by 24 November 2026.
rewordings: The standing order has to be raised by 24 November 2026.
Deadline for the quarterly order of flow cells and reagents: 24 Nov 2026.
The recurring indent for flow cells must be raised before 24 November 2026, not after.
hardRewordings: The quarterly paperwork for cells and reagents has to go in a fortnight before the next slot at the core.

facts.fact: For the standing order the PI signs the indent first, then the lab manager raises the purchase order.
rewordings: The PI signs the indent and only then does the lab manager raise the purchase order.
Nothing moves on the standing order until the indent is signed upstairs.
Order of steps: indent signed by the PI, purchase order raised by the lab manager.
hardRewordings: First the one who holds the budget puts a name on the form, then the office turns it into an order.

facts.fact: If the biosafety approval lapses all isolate work must stop, it stopped for two weeks last year, and a fresh inspection is needed before work restarts.
rewordings: A lapse in the biosafety approval stops all isolate work until a fresh inspection.
If the biosafety approval expires, isolate work stops for about two weeks as it did last time.
Isolate work must stop the moment the biosafety approval lapses, and restarts only after an inspection.
hardRewordings: Lose the committee sign off and the bench side of the project is frozen for a fortnight, with a visit before anyone starts again.

facts.fact: Imran Sheikh may have his progress review moved to January because the benchmark work is behind.
rewordings: Imran's progress review may move to January, the benchmark is behind.
The progress review for Imran Sheikh is likely to slip to January.
Imran is behind on the benchmark, so his progress review moves to January.
